messages:
alex: Quick one — noticed inconsistent behavior around stop sequences + max_tokens + logprobs. Sometimes responses come back with no `logprobs` even though `logprobs` was requested. Example request I sent below.

rina: Huh, I think I've seen that. Can you paste the request + response? short snippets are fine.

alex: Request payload (sanitized):
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-large",
  "prompt": "Write a short email...",
  "max_tokens": 50,
  "stop": ["\n\n"],
  "temperature": 0.7,
  "top_p": 0.9,
  "logprobs": 5
}
```
Response (truncated):
```json
{
  "id": "resp_123",
  "text": "Thanks for...",
  "finish_reason": "stop"
  // no logprobs field in some runs
}
```

josh_k: We should be clear about the contract: if user requests `logprobs`, we promise to return them unless the model runtime truly didn't compute them. The service shouldn't drop them in postprocessing.

samir: Two likely possibilities: 1) we short-circuit token streaming and skip computing logprobs for the last chunk, or 2) stop-match happens in decoded string space and we trim tokens after computing but forget to attach logprobs. Either is plausible.

maya: I suspect (2). Our tokenizer/stopping lives in postprocess. If stop triggered on substring match spanning token boundaries, we might drop tokens and accidentally drop `logprobs` payload assembly. I'll look at the postprocess code.

alex: Also curious about priority: if both `max_tokens` and `stop` are reached on the same step, what's canonical behavior? return tokens up to stop and mark finish_reason `stop` or `length`? I saw both in different runs.

rina: Spec we discussed: stop has higher precedence — if stop pattern matches at any point we mark `finish_reason: stop` and truncate at match. `max_tokens` only wins if token budget exhausted without any stop matching. But need to confirm edge-case tie.

josh_k: Agreed on spec. We should ensure deterministic ordering in runtime: detect stop AFTER token selection but BEFORE final trim, and set finish_reason accordingly. Also ensure `logprobs` includes tokens up to the stop token.

samir: I'll open an issue and add a minimal repro + CI test. Will link PR for runtime fix. (pinging @eng-runtime)

ci-bot: Created issue #3421: "gen: missing logprobs when stop truncates output (stop vs max_tokens edge)" — https://redwood/3421

maya: Quick note on temp/top_p: someone reported weird nondeterminism even with `temperature: 0`. If `top_p < 1` and `temperature == 0` our sampler sometimes uses top-p sampling codepath which can still be nondeterministic due to tie handling. The safer contract for deterministic/generative-greedy is `temperature: 0` AND `top_p: 1.0` or explicitly `best_of` style deterministic path.

alex: Good to call that out for docs. Customers assume `temp=0` -> deterministic. We should publish a small contract note: "temp=0 guarantees greedy decoding only when top_p=1.0" or similar.

rina: For workaround: if you need logprobs always, recommend `logprobs` + `temperature=0` + `top_p=1` until we patch. Also we've got to add unit tests that assert `logprobs` present when requested and `finish_reason` deterministic for tie cases.

josh_k: I'll add test cases: (a) stop matched within token, (b) stop and max_tokens on same token, (c) temp=0 + top_p<1 determinism check. Will send PR with tests and a small runtime patch to preserve logprobs assembly.

samir: Thanks — also can someone ping support to proactively notify any users who filed tickets on this? Might be a noisy regression for a small set of customers.

maya: I'll drop a note in #support after I open the PR.

alex: Awesome. Ping me when PR is up. :thumbsup:
